title: Skip Neighbors
commonMistakes: Taking every other element from index 0 without considering starting at index 1
Using a greedy rule that takes a value whenever it is larger than its neighbors
Forgetting that skipping a value does not force you to take the next one
followUps: How would you reconstruct which indices were chosen?
What changes if the values can be negative?
How would you handle a circular list where the first and last values are adjacent?
attribution: Original problem by the Base Case contributors.
